Let \(n\) be the number of pictures she takes.

Each picture fails with probability:
\[
1-\frac15=\frac45
\]
So the probability that none of the \(n\) pictures turn out is:
\[
\left(\frac45\right)^n
\]
Thus the probability that at least one turns out is:
\[
1-\left(\frac45\right)^n
\]
We need:
\[
1-\left(\frac45\right)^n \ge \frac34
\]
\[
\left(\frac45\right)^n \le \frac14
\]
Taking logarithms:
\[
n \ln\left(\frac45\right) \le \ln\left(\frac14\right)
\]
Since \(\ln(4/5)<0\), dividing flips the inequality:
\[
n \ge \frac{\ln(1/4)}{\ln(4/5)} \approx 6.21
\]
So the smallest integer \(n\) is \(7\).

The answer is 7.
